question: A pleomorphic adenoma of the parotid can be safely enucleated (shelled out along its capsule) because it has a well-defined, intact capsule.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct. Pleomorphic adenoma has microscopic capsular pseudopod extensions — enucleation invariably leaves residual tumour, causing high recurrence rates. Superficial parotidectomy (with cuff of normal tissue) is mandatory.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This is false. Although it appears well-encapsulated, a pleomorphic adenoma has microscopic pseudopod projections that breach the capsule. Simple enucleation leaves these behind and carries a recurrence rate of 20–45%. Superficial or total parotidectomy with preservation of the facial nerve is the correct procedure.
